g.text: ⇒ mark w DEAD, reclaim its tasks (see below)
(60s > one ~30s GIL-bound MAP, so a busy healthy worker is never wrongly killed;
a real crash closes the TCP socket and is detected instantly regardless)
MAP tasks ≫ workers for huge data (e.g. 1000 tasks / 50 nodes)
each mapper: read (NFS) → map → partition hash(k')%R
write buckets to LOCAL /tmp/mr/part-i-j.tmp then rename → part-i-j (ATOMIC)
(idempotent: a MAP_DONE for an already-DONE task is ignored)
m1 was IN_PROGRESS → reset to IDLE
(also: every COMPLETED map owned by N1 → reset to IDLE,
re-executes m1 on a live node
when ≈95% of MAP tasks DONE and m2 still slow:
launch a BACKUP attempt of m2 on an idle node
Main builds routing table from METADATA only (no data read by Main)
For reducer j: peers = [(host_i, port_i, part-i-j) ∀ i]
══ Phase 2 — REDUCE + SHUFFLE (pull, with location repair) ══
SHUFFLE = N×N direct worker↔worker FETCH; Main uninvolved
fetched bytes merged into IN-MEMORY map (idempotent: re-fetch is safe)
if N0 DEAD ⇒ re-run its map m0 (attempt+1) on a live node,
then reply with the NEW location (paper: notify reducers of re-exec)
reduce: sum counts per key → sort → top-K
r1 IN_PROGRESS → reset to IDLE, attempt+1
(reduce output committed atomically ⇒ if out-1 already renamed, r1 is DONE
new reducer RE-FETCHES all part-i-1 from mappers
Main reads ~/out/out-0..out-(R-1) (atomic, exactly-once), merges → global top-100
Main checkpoints state every C seconds to ~/mr/master.ckpt.
On Main restart: reload checkpoint, re-probe workers via STATUS_QUERY,
resume from last barrier instead of restarting the whole job.
[independent scenario: a source mapper host died AFTER shuffle began]
[independent scenario: N1 (a reducer) crashes before REDUCE_DONE]
